description: A compromised release is usually caught and pulled within days, so propose a version only once it passes minimumReleaseAge. A version without a release timestamp counts as too new. Both behaviors are set explicitly so that a change to Renovate's defaults can't weaken them.
Every update is a chore, so a changelog built from commit types leaves it out.
Actions and Docker images are pinned to a digest, so a moved tag can't change what runs. Renovate updates the digest and its version comment together.

Updates merge on their own once they pass minimumReleaseAge and every status check, so a repository nobody works on still gets fixes. A major update can break the code that uses it, so it waits for review.
